root_cause: The modal's click listener uses `event.target.closest('[data-micromodal-close]')` to detect clicks on the backdrop or close buttons. Because the backdrop element is an ancestor of all inner content, any click inside the modal (including on checkboxes) matches and triggers `closeModal`, causing the modal to close unexpectedly when interacting with form controls via keyboard or mouse.
repair_strategy: Replace the `closest` check with a direct `hasAttribute` test on the event target. This ensures only the backdrop overlay, close button, or done button themselves—each of which carries the `data-micromodal-close` attribute—can close the modal, while interactions with inner elements (e.g., checkboxes) no longer mistakenly close it.
expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Space on a checkbox inside the preferences dialog will now toggle the checkbox without closing the dialog, allowing keyboard users to adjust newsletter preferences as intended. The dialog remains open until the user explicitly activates the backdrop, close button, or Done button.
functional_risks: If any inner element erroneously gains the `data-micromodal-close` attribute, it would unintentionally close the modal; however, no such elements exist in the current markup.
The change does not affect backdrop or programmatic close mechanisms, as those elements retain the attribute and will still trigger closure.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Space on the #weekly checkbox toggles its checked state and the modal's `aria-hidden` remains false.
Verify that clicking the backdrop, the × button, or the Done button still closes the modal and returns focus to the trigger button.
Verify that focus management after closing (returning to the trigger) continues to work correctly.
